title: Reconstruction: Holding Several Contracts at Once
content:
**Clause.** A customer may hold any number of Reconstruction contracts at once, one per property or unit being rebuilt; landlords, property managers and associations commonly hold several, one per damaged unit. Each contract carries its own draws, change orders, balance and warranty.

## What the clause settles

| Question the desk meets | Answer under the clause |
|---|---|
| Is there a cap on how many Reconstruction contracts one customer holds? | No. The company sets no maximum number of contracts per customer. |
| What is one contract written for? | One property, or one unit, being rebuilt. |
| Do two contracts of the same customer share a balance? | No. Each contract keeps its own balance. |
| Do draws, change orders or the warranty pass from one contract to another? | No. Each contract carries its own draws, change orders and warranty. |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A property manager whose building has three damaged units may hold three Reconstruction contracts, one per unit. A draw requested on the first unit's contract is a draw of that contract only; a change order signed on the second unit's contract changes only that contract; the warranty of the third unit's contract runs on that contract alone.
